scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's tackle this scenario. The user is asking if they're in the wrong (AITA) for visiting their 19-year-old son unannounced. The son has been ignoring them for two months, only replying occasionally with excuses. The parent went to the city for another reason, tried calling but couldn't reach, so they went to the apartment. The son's place was messy, and he was annoyed about the unannounced visit.

First, I need to evaluate the moral acceptability of the parent's action. The key points here are the son's age (19, so an adult), the parent's concern due to the son's ignoring, and the unannounced visit. 

On one hand, the son is an adult and has the right to his own space. Ignoring a parent isn't necessarily wrong, especially if the son is busy with studies. The parent's action of visiting without prior contact could be seen as intrusive. The son's reaction of being annoyed and pointing out the lack of notice supports that. 

On the other hand, the parent might be worried about their son's well-being, given the neglect of the living space. The messiness could indicate neglect, which might be a concern for the parent. However, the parent didn't address the mess directly; they just made a joke. 

The moral acceptability hinges on whether the unannounced visit was justified. Since the son is an adult, respecting his autonomy is important. The parent's approach might have been well-intentioned but could have been handled better by communicating first. The son's response indicates that the visit was unwelcome, which leans towards the action being morally unacceptable. 

So, the answer is 0 because the unannounced visit disregarded the son's autonomy and caused annoyance, even if the parent's intentions were good.
